background.$description: Page/document ground — the lowest surface everything sits on. Recessed slightly below the white --card so cards/panels lift off the page by ground offset (ΔL≈0.022). See research/structural-design 08 §H + #187.

card.$description: Card/panel surface raised off the page ground.

primary.$description: Brand accent — primary action fill (buttons, active state).

primary-text.$description: On-surface brand-accent TEXT color; ≥4.5:1 on content surfaces.

accent.$description: Subtle accent surface (hover rows, highlighted cells).

destructive-text.$description: On-surface error TEXT color; ≥4.5:1 on content surfaces AND on those surfaces' composited bg-destructive/10 wash (#38 — darkened from 0.555 so the pairing every wash-based badge actually ships stays AA, not just the bare surface).

success.$description: Success/positive fill. #406 — DEEPENED out of the L 0.6 dead zone so the whole :root status family carries ONE ink polarity (white), the same move #381 made for --warning. Deepening only RAISES the mark-surface rung: 4.60:1 at worst (was 3.36:1).

success-foreground.$description: Ink on a --success fill. #406 — back to white, matching --primary/--destructive/--warning/--info here. The earlier dark ink (#321/#383) was the other way out of the L 0.6 dead zone, but it left :root's five status plates split across two ink polarities. 4.95:1.

success-text.$description: On-surface success TEXT color; ≥4.5:1 on content surfaces AND on those surfaces' composited bg-success/10 wash (#38 — darkened from 0.515 so the pairing every wash-based badge actually ships stays AA, not just the bare surface).

warning.$description: Warning/caution fill. Burnt orange: a colour-only warning mark must clear WCAG 1.4.11 (≥3:1) on every content surface (#381), and at the authored amber's hue 70 that bar forces a lightness/chroma pair that reads brown — hue 55 buys chroma at the same lightness.

warning-foreground.$description: Ink on a --warning fill. Dark, because the fill is bright enough that light ink is sub-AA (3.45:1) — the one status plate here whose ink polarity is reversed.

warning-text.$description: On-surface warning TEXT color; ≥4.5:1 on content surfaces AND on those surfaces' composited bg-warning/10 wash (#38 — darkened from 0.53 so the pairing every wash-based badge actually ships stays AA, not just the bare surface).

info.$description: Informational fill. #406 — DEEPENED out of the L 0.6 dead zone for the same one-polarity reason as --success. Mark-surface rung rises to 4.68:1 at worst (was 3.42:1).

info-foreground.$description: Ink on an --info fill. #406 — back to white, matching the rest of the :root status family. 5.03:1.

info-text.$description: On-surface info TEXT color; ≥4.5:1 on content surfaces AND on those surfaces' composited bg-info/10 wash (#38 — darkened from 0.525 so the pairing every wash-based badge actually ships stays AA, not just the bare surface).

border.$description: Subtle/redundant hairline boundary (the default border color).

input.$description: Form-control outline on the SUBTLE hairline rung (== --border) per ADR 0010 amendment (2026-06-20). Resting <3:1 is an accepted internal-use tradeoff — field identity rests on the recessed fill + focus ring + control glyphs + hover.

ring.$description: Focus ring color. DEEPER + more saturated than --primary on purpose (#385): the two were byte-identical, so 'this control is focused' and 'this is the primary action' were one signal. Same move light already made for its own ring. ΔE(OKLab) 0.104 from --primary and 0.178 from --info; 7.42:1 vs --background.

surface.$description: Layered neutral surface for shells/panels. Recessed to match --background (08 §H / #187).

sidebar.$description: App-chrome sidebar ground. Recessed BELOW the content canvas (--background 0.978) so chrome reads as the most-recessed app-frame surface: chrome(0.955) < canvas(0.978) < card(1.0). ΔL≈0.023 vs canvas is a clearly perceptible elevation step.

sidebar-border.$description: Sidebar border/divider. Deepened a hairline step as --sidebar recessed so the divider stays visible against the recessed chrome ground.

sidebar-accent.$description: Sidebar hover/active surface. Deepened so hover/selected stays perceptible (ΔL≈0.04) against the recessed --sidebar (0.955).

sidebar-primary-foreground.$description: Ink on --sidebar-primary. #406/#385 — a DECLARED mirror of --primary-foreground, the partner of the --sidebar-primary: var(--primary) alias. It was a duplicated literal, which cannot be told apart from an accidental collision and drifts the moment one side is retuned.

flow-node-foreground.$description: Text color on a flow node.

chat-user.$description: AI chat — user message bubble surface.

chat-user-foreground.$description: Text color on a user message bubble.

chat-assistant.$description: AI chat — assistant message bubble surface.

chat-assistant-foreground.$description: Text color on an assistant message bubble.

chart-1.$description: Categorical data series 1. A lighter, chart-tuned cousin of the brand accent rather than a copy of it (#385): as a byte-identical duplicate of --primary/--ring it was also the darkest, highest-contrast member of its own ramp (5.02:1 vs --card against 2.87-4.37 for the rest) — never tuned as a ramp step. Now 3.73:1, evening the ramp, and ΔE 0.175 from --ring.

calc-foreground.$description: Calc syntax: default token color (plain identifiers, punctuation).

calc-unit.$description: Calc syntax: unit suffix color (px, %, em, …).

calc-currency.$description: Calc syntax: currency / monetary value color.

calc-variable.$description: Calc syntax: variable / definition name color.

calc-reference.$description: Calc syntax: reference to another field / cell color.

calc-result.$description: Calc syntax: computed result / answer emphasis color.

calc-warning.$description: Calc syntax: warning / unresolved reference color (error hue).

code-function.$description: CodeBlock syntax: function / call name color.

code-type.$description: CodeBlock syntax: type / class name color.

code-tag.$description: CodeBlock syntax: markup tag color. Its own hue — deliberately NOT --calc-warning/--destructive-text's red-orange, so a valid <tag> never reads as an error (#315 follow-up).
